keyWhy.ko: 핵심은 «같은 피가 몸속을 빙글빙글 계속 돈다(발견)» 와 «심장은 같은 피를 끝없는 여행에 내보내는 지칠 줄 모르는 펌프다(결론)» 입니다. 초록색 문장이 정답이에요.
keyWhy.en: The key ideas are the discovery (the same blood travels around the body again and again in a circle) and the conclusion (the heart is a tireless pump that sends the same blood on an endless journey). The green sentences are the answers.

boxes.a: The same blood travels around the body in a circle

boxes.qen: How does the heart move blood?
boxes.a: The right side sends it to the lungs; the left side sends it to the body

qs.q: Why did Harvey think the old idea about blood did not make sense?
qs.qko: 하비가 피에 대한 옛 생각이 말이 안 된다고 본 이유는 무엇인가요?
opts: Because the heart pushes out far too much blood for the body to make in one day
Because he saw that the heart stops at night
Because blood is used up like fuel in a car
evs: The amount was far too large for the body to make in a single day.
For more than a thousand years, doctors believed that the body made new blood every day and used it up like fuel.
It is a muscle about the size of your fist, and it has four chambers.
Your heart beats about 100,000 times a day without ever taking a break.
why: 하비가 계산해 보니, 심장이 내보내는 피의 양이 몸이 하루 만에 만들기에는 너무 많았다고 했어요.
Harvey found that the amount of blood the heart pushes out was far too large for the body to make in a single day.

qs.q: In "without ever taking a break," what does "taking a break" mean?
qs.qko: «without ever taking a break» 에서 «taking a break» 는 무슨 뜻인가요?
evs: Your heart beats about 100,000 times a day without ever taking a break.
The heart is the pump that makes this possible.
The right side sends blood to the lungs to pick up oxygen.
An English doctor named William Harvey thought this idea did not make sense.
why: 심장은 하루에 약 10만 번이나 뛰면서 한 번도 «쉬지 않는다» 고 했어요. «take a break» 는 잠깐 멈추고 쉬는 거예요.
The heart beats about 100,000 times a day and never stops, so «taking a break» means stopping to rest.

qs.q: How does the heart send blood to the lungs and to the body?
qs.qko: 심장은 피를 폐와 온몸으로 어떻게 보내나요?
opts: The right side sends blood to the lungs for oxygen, and the left side pumps it to the body
Both sides send blood only to the brain
The lungs pump blood back into the stomach
evs: The right side sends blood to the lungs to pick up oxygen.
He calculated how much blood the heart pushes out with each beat.
The left side then pumps that oxygen-rich blood to the rest of the body.
Your heart beats about 100,000 times a day without ever taking a break.
why: 오른쪽은 피를 폐로 보내 산소를 얻게 하고, 왼쪽은 그 산소가 풍부한 피를 온몸으로 보낸다고 했어요. 두 문장을 함께 봐야 해요.
The right side sends blood to the lungs to pick up oxygen, and the left side pumps that oxygen-rich blood to the rest of the body. You need both sentences.

ends: How can exercise make our hearts stronger?
운동은 어떻게 우리 심장을 튼튼하게 할까요?
How do our lungs bring oxygen into our bodies?
우리 폐는 어떻게 몸속에 산소를 들여올까요?

write.src: “It is important to <u>take care of our hearts</u> because <u>they work all day without a break</u>.”
write.howtoKo: 예문을 틀로 삼아, 빈칸 두 곳을 «중요한 일 + 그 이유» 로 바꿔 영어로 써 보세요.
write.howtoEn: Use the example as a pattern. Write something important and the reason in English.
write.moreKo: 한 걸음 더: «because» 뒤에 «누가 + 무엇을» 넣어 이유를 분명하게 써 보세요. (예: because our hearts never rest)
write.moreEn: One more step: after «because», write who + what to make your reason clear. (e.g. because our hearts never rest)
